info.title: Mediflow API
info.description: Generated from the API route schemas by `pnpm gen:api`. Do not edit by hand.

mfaEnabled.description: Whether sign-in asks for an authenticator code.

activeTenant.description: Null until a user with several hospitals picks one.

policy.description: Null when there is no active tenant.

needsPassword.description: False when this person already has an account: they only accept.

secret.description: Base32, for typing into an authenticator by hand.

recoveryCodes.description: One-time codes. Returned this once and never again.

primary.description: Brand colour as six-digit hex. Must read as text on a white background (contrast of at least 4.5:1); the web app falls back to its default colour otherwise.

logoUrl.description: https or same-origin URL of the hospital logo (SVG or WebP, at most 50 kB).

features.description: Module flags. A module that is absent is off.

idleTimeoutMinutes.description: A session with no activity for this long ends. The web app warns shortly before and signs the user out. Absent means the app default.

status.description: A suspended hospital keeps its data but its staff cannot use the app. Tenant-scoped routes answer 403 tenant_suspended.

Invite.description: An invitation that has been emailed. The link is not returned.

StaffMember.description: Someone who works at the hospital, or has been invited to. For a member `id` is the user id; for an invitation it is the invitation id.

StaffPage.description: Cursor envelope used by every list endpoint.

PatientSummary.description: A patient as shown in a list: compact, no clinical data.

phone.description: Masked to its last four digits for a caller without patient.contact:read.

PatientPage.description: Cursor envelope used by every list endpoint.

PatientRecord.description: A registered patient with the details captured at registration. Email and address are left out for a caller without patient.contact:read.

phone.description: Masked to its last four digits for a caller without patient.contact:read.

version.description: Goes up by one each time the record changes. Send it back as expectedVersion when changing the record.

PatientUpdate.description: The version the change is based on, and the fields to change. Null clears an optional field. The MRN never changes.

expectedVersion.description: The version of the record the change was made from. If the record has changed since, the request is refused with 409 conflict and nothing is changed.

PatientDuplicateMatch.description: A possible duplicate, masked by the server: enough to recognise the person, not to read their details. No id.

Department.description: A department of one hospital. Holds no patient data.

version.description: Counts the changes. Sent back as expectedVersion.

DepartmentPage.description: Cursor envelope used by every list endpoint.

Doctor.description: A doctor profile: a staff member of one hospital, in one department. Holds no patient data.

active.description: False once the doctor no longer practises here, or while their membership of the hospital is deactivated: kept on old records, not offered for new ones.

version.description: Counts the changes. Sent back as expectedVersion.

DoctorPage.description: Cursor envelope used by every list endpoint.

consultationMinutes.description: The usual length of one appointment.
The usual length of one appointment.

DoctorCandidate.description: A user who works at the hospital and has no doctor profile there. The email tells namesakes apart; nothing else of the account is given.

DoctorCandidatePage.description: Cursor envelope used by every list endpoint.

DoctorAvailability.description: Regular weekly working hours. A day without a session is a day off.

ServicePrice.description: What a service costs on one price list from one date. A price is never edited: a new one takes over from its own date.

amountMinor.description: In the minor unit of the hospital's currency.

effectiveFrom.description: A calendar date at the hospital.

effectiveTo.description: The last day it applies. Absent while no later price follows.

ServicePricePage.description: Cursor envelope used by every list endpoint.

Service.description: Something the hospital can charge for. Holds no patient data. Its name, category and tax class can be changed, and a charge keeps what they were when it was posted: changing them never changes an old bill. `currentPrice` is the price in force today on the standard list, absent when there is none.

code.description: The service's identity on bills. Never changes.

taxClass.description: Which tax rate applies, as a class. The rate of each class is the hospital's tax setting, so a change of rate does not touch the services.

version.description: Counts the changes. Sent back as expectedVersion.

ServicePage.description: Cursor envelope used by every list endpoint.

taxClass.description: Which tax rate applies, as a class. The rate of each class is the hospital's tax setting, so a change of rate does not touch the services.

priceMinor.description: In the minor unit of the hospital's currency.

taxClass.description: Which tax rate applies, as a class. The rate of each class is the hospital's tax setting, so a change of rate does not touch the services.

cursor.description: Opaque. Pass the nextCursor of the previous page.

archived.description: True lists the archived services instead of the active ones. Absent: false.

amountMinor.description: In the minor unit of the hospital's currency.

effectiveFrom.description: A calendar date at the hospital.

standard.description: The list used when none is named.

Drug.description: A medicine or a consumable the hospital keeps. What the item is, not what it costs or how much is in stock: those belong to the pharmacy and its batches. Holds no patient data.

type.description: A medicine, or a consumable such as gloves or a syringe.

genericName.description: The generic name of a medicine, or what a consumable is.

strength.description: As written on the pack: "500 mg".

unit.description: What one unit of stock is: "strip of 10", "100 ml bottle", "piece".

schedule.description: The drug schedule the item falls under, recorded as a class. What each schedule requires (registers, prescriptions kept) is the pharmacy module's to enforce.

controlled.description: Whether it is handled as a controlled drug. Always true for schedule x and narcotic, whatever is sent.

reorderLevel.description: Stock at or below this many units is low. Absent: no level set.

version.description: Counts the changes. Sent back as expectedVersion.

DrugPage.description: Cursor envelope used by every list endpoint.

type.description: A medicine, or a consumable such as gloves or a syringe.

genericName.description: The generic name of a medicine, or what a consumable is.

strength.description: As written on the pack: "500 mg".

unit.description: What one unit of stock is: "strip of 10", "100 ml bottle", "piece".

schedule.description: The drug schedule the item falls under, recorded as a class. What each schedule requires (registers, prescriptions kept) is the pharmacy module's to enforce.

controlled.description: Whether it is handled as a controlled drug. Always true for schedule x and narcotic, whatever is sent.

reorderLevel.description: Stock at or below this many units is low. Absent or null: no level.

strength.description: As written on the pack: "500 mg".

unit.description: What one unit of stock is: "strip of 10", "100 ml bottle", "piece".

schedule.description: The drug schedule the item falls under, recorded as a class. What each schedule requires (registers, prescriptions kept) is the pharmacy module's to enforce.

controlled.description: Whether it is handled as a controlled drug. Always true for schedule x and narcotic, whatever is sent.

reorderLevel.description: Null removes the level. An empty brand, strength or unit removes that too.

cursor.description: Opaque. Pass the nextCursor of the previous page.

archived.description: True lists the archived items instead of the active ones. Absent: false.

genericName.description: The generic name of a medicine, or what a consumable is.

LabTest.description: A test or a panel the laboratory offers: what it is, how it is collected and how its result is read. Holds no patient data.

code.description: The test's identity on orders and reports. Never changes.

kind.description: A single test, or a panel: a named set of tests ordered together (a lipid profile). A panel has components and no result of its own.

resultType.description: How a result is recorded: a number against a reference range, or text (positive, negative, a description). For a panel it means nothing.

unit.description: The unit of a numeric result: g/dL.

container.description: What the sample is collected in.

turnaroundHours.description: How long a result usually takes from collection.

serviceName.description: The name of the linked service, when there is one. The name alone is shown to everyone who may read the test, by decision; nothing else of the service (a price, a tax class) is ever added here.

components.description: The tests of a panel. Empty for a single test.

version.description: Counts the changes. Sent back as expectedVersion.

LabTestPage.description: Cursor envelope used by every list endpoint.

kind.description: A single test, or a panel: a named set of tests ordered together (a lipid profile). A panel has components and no result of its own.

resultType.description: How a result is recorded: a number against a reference range, or text (positive, negative, a description). For a panel it means nothing.

unit.description: The unit of a numeric result: g/dL.

container.description: What the sample is collected in.

turnaroundHours.description: How long a result usually takes from collection.

serviceId.description: The service the test is charged as: a laboratory service of the same hospital's catalog. Empty text removes the link on a change.

componentIds.description: The single tests of a panel, in the order they are reported.

LabAge.description: An age as it is written: a value with its unit. Never turned into a count of days: a patient reaches it on the calendar day that lies that long after the date of birth, so leap years and the lengths of months are respected. At most 150 years, in any unit.

LabRange.description: What is normal for one sex in one span of age: from `ageFrom`, included (the day the patient reaches it), until `ageUntil`, not included (that day belongs to the next range). No `ageUntil`: no upper age.

sex.description: Whom the row is for. A row for one sex is used before a row for any.

low.description: The lowest normal value. Absent: no lower limit.

high.description: The highest normal value. Absent: no upper limit.

criticalLow.description: At or below this the result is critical. Never above `low`.

criticalHigh.description: At or above this the result is critical. Never below `high`.

LabRangeResolved.description: `range` is absent when no row covers that age and sex.

BedCategory.description: A class of bed (general ward, private room, intensive care), which decides what a day in it is charged as. The charge itself is posted by the admissions module from the linked service, at the price in force that day. An admission keeps the category and the service of its bed as they were when the patient was given it, so a change made here applies to stays that start after it.

serviceName.description: The name of the linked service, when there is one. The name alone is shown to everyone who may read wards, by decision; nothing else of the service (a price, a tax class) is ever added here.

bedCount.description: The beds in use that have this category.

version.description: Counts the changes. Sent back as expectedVersion.

BedCategoryPage.description: Cursor envelope used by every list endpoint.

serviceId.description: The bed-day service a day in a bed of this category is charged as: a service of the same hospital's catalog in its bed category. Empty text removes the link on a change.
The bed-day service a day in a bed of this category is charged as: a service of the same hospital's catalog in its bed category. Empty text removes the link on a change.

Ward.description: A ward of the hospital. Holds no patient data.

code.description: Short and unique in the hospital. Never changes.

version.description: Counts the changes. Sent back as expectedVersion.

WardPage.description: Cursor envelope used by every list endpoint.

floor.description: Where it is: a floor, a block, a wing.

departmentId.description: The department the ward belongs to, when it belongs to one. Empty text removes it on a change.

floor.description: Where it is: a floor, a block, a wing.

departmentId.description: The department the ward belongs to, when it belongs to one. Empty text removes it on a change.

Bed.description: A bed. Its status says whether it can take a patient; who is in it is the admission module, never here.

status.description: available: free to take a patient. occupied: a patient is admitted to it (set by admissions). cleaning: being made ready after a discharge (set by housekeeping). blocked: taken out of use here, with a reason.

blockedNote.description: A few words more about why. About the bed, never about a patient.

version.description: Counts the changes. Sent back as expectedVersion.
Counts the changes. Sent back as expectedVersion.

WardDetail.description: A ward with its rooms and their beds, archived ones included.

number.description: What is written on the bed: unique in its ward.
What is written on the bed: unique in its ward.

note.description: A few words more: about the bed, never about a patient. Free text, so the API treats it as possibly sensitive: it is not written to logs or to event payloads.

Code.description: A diagnosis code (ICD-10) or a procedure code. Reference data shared by every hospital, so it carries no tenant; only `favourite` is the hospital’s own.

code.description: As it is written: A09, E11.9.

favourite.description: Whether the active tenant marked it.

CodePage.description: Cursor envelope used by every list endpoint.

favourites.description: True gives the favourites only. Absent: false.

cursor.description: Opaque. Pass the nextCursor of the previous page.

Template.description: A document template of a hospital. Holds no patient data.

TemplatePage.description: Cursor envelope used by every list endpoint.

savedByName.description: The member of staff who saved it.

redactedAt.description: When the name and the text of this version were removed. Absent otherwise.

TemplateVersion.description: One version of a template, as it was saved. A redacted version has an empty name and an empty text, and says when, by whom and why.

savedByName.description: The member of staff who saved it.

redactedAt.description: When the name and the text of this version were removed. Absent otherwise.

body.description: The text of a template: the rich text document of the app (paragraphs, headings, lists, quotes and marks), never HTML. Reduced to that allowlist on the way in. Placeholders are plain text in double braces, `{{patient.name}}`. A placeholder is recognised only inside one run of text, for the check and for filling alike: one that is split by formatting (half of it bold) is neither checked nor ever filled, by any part of the system. Names are trimmed and case-sensitive. A value is filled in as text and is never read for placeholders again.

reason.description: Why the version is removed, from a list: free text here could repeat what is being removed.

type.description: How the text becomes the value: `boolean` is yes or no (true, false, y, n, 1, 0); `enum` one of `values`, whatever its capitals; `date` YYYY-MM-DD; `amount` the hospital currency with a point before the minor units, grouped by commas or not.

ImportBatch.description: Records of one kind loaded from a file. It holds counts and codes, never a value of a row.

status.description: staging: rows are being sent. checking: the dry run is running. checked: it has run, and the batch can be written when problemCount is 0. queued, running: being written. committed: every row was written. failed: nothing was written. cancelled: given up, or left unfinished for a week.

doneCount.description: Rows checked while checking, rows written while running.

failure.description: Why nothing was written, as a code: rows_refused (see the problems), permission_withdrawn, write_failed, expired.

ImportBatchPage.description: Cursor envelope used by every list endpoint.

ImportRowsUpload.description: Rows of the file, as many requests as it takes. A line sent twice is kept as it was first sent.

fields.description: The fields of the kind the columns of the file were mapped to, in the order of `values`. Each at most once.

values.description: The text of each field of `fields`. An empty text is no value.

ImportProblem.description: Never the value that was refused.

code.description: What is wrong. Of one field: required, not_a_whole_number, not_yes_or_no, not_allowed, not_a_date, not_an_amount, too_many_decimals, invalid, not_found, out_of_range, too_few_digits, not_an_email. Of a row: duplicate_in_file, or the code its create route answers with (drug_exists, service_code_taken, lab_test_code_taken, patient_possible_duplicate, validation_failed).

ImportProblemPage.description: Cursor envelope used by every list endpoint.

NoticePage.description: Cursor envelope used by every list endpoint.

userAgent.description: The browser as it described itself at sign-in, for the person to recognise the device.

current.description: True for the session making this call.

AppointmentSummary.description: An appointment as a list shows it: when, with whom, for whom and its status. Not the whole record: the reason is not in a list.

departmentName.description: The doctor's department. Absent when it has none.

AppointmentPage.description: Cursor envelope used by every list endpoint.

get.description: The active hospital of the session and its configuration. Private per session, never CDN-cached.

200.description: Default Response

post.description: Signs in with email and password and starts a session, returned as an httpOnly cookie. Every failure of the email and password has the same answer, 401 invalid_credentials. An account with an authenticator answers 401 mfa_required until the request also carries `code`, and 401 invalid_mfa_code when the code is wrong.

code.description: Authenticator code, or a recovery code. Only for accounts that have one.

200.description: Default Response

post.description: Ends the session, on the server and in the browser. Succeeds whether or not there was one.

get.description: Bootstraps the app in one request: the signed-in user, the active tenant with its config, and the effective access policy. Private per session, never CDN-cached. Session routes ignore X-Tenant-ID, so a stale tab can always reload its session.

200.description: Default Response

post.description: Rebinds the session to another hospital the user belongs to and returns the new session. Affects every tab.

200.description: Default Response

post.description: What the invite screen shows before the person accepts: which hospital, which email, and whether a password has to be chosen. The token is in the body, not the URL, so it is not logged.

200.description: Default Response

post.description: Accepts an invite. Someone new sets their password here (400 password_required without one). Someone with an account needs only the token. The link works once. The person then signs in.
Emails a reset link if the address has an account. The answer is the same either way, so it cannot be used to find accounts.

204.description: Done, whether or not an email is sent

post.description: Sets a new password with a reset link. The link works once. Every session of the user ends.
Starts setting up an authenticator app and returns its secret. Sign-in does not change until a code is confirmed. Calling it again before that starts over.

200.description: Default Response

post.description: Finishes setup with a code from the authenticator. From now on sign-in asks for a code. Returns the recovery codes, once.

200.description: Default Response

post.description: Replaces the recovery codes. Needs the password and a code from the authenticator itself.

200.description: Default Response

post.description: Removes the authenticator and its recovery codes. Needs the password and a current code.

get.description: Whether the active hospital requires an authenticator of its staff (its `mfa` and `mfa_required` switches are both on). A user for whom this is true and whose `mfaEnabled` is false is refused every route of the hospital with `mfa_required` until one is set up.

200.description: Default Response

get.description: The effective access policy for the active tenant. Supports ETag and If-None-Match so a refresh is cheap. The answer is `Cache-Control: private, no-store`: the client keeps the policy and its ETag itself, and no browser keeps a copy. Returns 409 tenant_mismatch when X-Tenant-ID differs from the session tenant.

200.description: The current policy

get.description: Liveness check. The process is running.

200.description: Default Response

get.description: Readiness check. The process can reach its database.

200.description: Default Response

post.description: Invites someone to the active hospital in one of its roles and emails them a single-use link. A newer invite to the same address replaces an older one. The role may hold nothing the caller does not hold: 403 role_not_allowed otherwise.

parameters.name: idempotency-key
parameters.description: A unique value (such as a UUID) chosen by the client. Repeating the request with the same key returns the first result instead of doing the work again.

201.description: An invitation that has been emailed. The link is not returned.

get.description: The people of the active tenant, by name: its members, or the invitations it has sent that are still open. `q` matches the name or the email address. The hospital is the session's. `total` comes with the first page.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: Opaque. Pass the nextCursor of the previous page.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: Which people: active members (when left out), deactivated members, or open invitations.

200.description: Cursor envelope used by every list endpoint.

get.description: The roles of the active tenant that the caller may invite someone into, by name: those whose permissions are all held by the caller's own role, so an invitation never grants more than the inviter has (POST /invites refuses the others with 403 role_not_allowed). Ids and names only: what a role may do belongs to role management.

200.description: Default Response

post.description: Deactivates someone's membership of the hospital: every session they have there ends at once, the open invitations they sent are withdrawn, and they cannot work there until reactivated. Their account and their memberships of other hospitals are untouched, and the membership is kept, never deleted. 409 cannot_deactivate_self for the caller's own membership, 409 last_admin when no other active member could manage staff. Doing it twice changes nothing. Nobody acts above themselves: a member whose role holds a permission the caller's role does not is refused with 403 role_not_allowed. Someone who is not a member of the hospital answers 404 staff_not_found, the same as a user that does not exist.

200.description: Someone who works at the hospital, or has been invited to. For a member `id` is the user id; for an invitation it is the invitation id.

post.description: Makes a deactivated membership active again, in the role it had. Doing it twice changes nothing. Nobody acts above themselves: a member whose role holds a permission the caller's role does not is refused with 403 role_not_allowed. Someone who is not a member of the hospital answers 404 staff_not_found, the same as a user that does not exist.

200.description: Someone who works at the hospital, or has been invited to. For a member `id` is the user id; for an invitation it is the invitation id.

post.description: Ends every session the person has at this hospital, so they must sign in again to work here: the sessions bound to it are revoked (`revoked` counts them), and a session they have at the hospital picker or at another hospital can no longer be brought here. Their work at other hospitals carries on. For the caller's own account only the sessions bound here are ended, and the current one is kept. Nobody acts above themselves: a member whose role holds a permission the caller's role does not is refused with 403 role_not_allowed. Someone who is not a member of the hospital answers 404 staff_not_found, the same as a user that does not exist.

200.description: Default Response

delete.description: Withdraws an open invitation: its link stops working. For an address that was wrong, since inviting again only sends the same address a new link. An invitation that is not open here (accepted, withdrawn, expired, another hospital's, unknown) answers 404 invite_not_found. The caller must be allowed to give its role (403 role_not_allowed).

post.description: Patients of the active hospital, one cursor page at a time. The search term travels in the body, never in a query string, because it can be a name, a phone number or an MRN. Every word of the term must appear in the name or MRN, in any order; a term that looks like a phone number is also matched against phone numbers for a caller who holds patient.contact:read. It reads data only. `total` is given on the first page.

q.description: Search text: name, phone or MRN.

cursor.description: Opaque. Pass the nextCursor of the previous page.

200.description: Cursor envelope used by every list endpoint.

post.description: Finds existing patients who may be the same person as one about to be registered, across the whole hospital. The identifying details travel in the body, never in a query string. Matches are masked and carry no id. It reads data only.

200.description: Default Response

post.description: Registers a patient in the active hospital and assigns the MRN. The Idempotency-Key header is required: a retried or double-submitted request returns the first result instead of a second patient. A replay answers with the id only; read the record to show it. The server records when and by whom contact consent was captured. While a batch of patients is being written from a file, a registration waits a few seconds and then answers 503 busy with Retry-After.

parameters.name: idempotency-key
parameters.description: A unique value (such as a UUID) chosen by the client. Repeating the request with the same key returns the first result instead of doing the work again.

201.description: A registered patient with the details captured at registration. Email and address are left out for a caller without patient.contact:read.

get.description: One patient of the active hospital, with the details captured at registration.

200.description: A registered patient with the details captured at registration. Email and address are left out for a caller without patient.contact:read.

patch.description: Changes registration details of a patient. expectedVersion is the version the caller read: if the record has changed since, the answer is 409 conflict and nothing is changed. Only the fields sent are changed; null clears email or address. The MRN and the hospital never change. Sending a contactConsent that differs from the one on record records the new decision with the time and the caller. Values the record already has change nothing.

200.description: A registered patient with the details captured at registration. Email and address are left out for a caller without patient.contact:read.

get.description: Departments of the active tenant, by name. Archived departments are listed only when asked for. `total` comes with the first page.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: Opaque. Pass the nextCursor of the previous page.

parameters.name: archived
parameters.description: True lists the archived departments instead of the active ones.

200.description: Cursor envelope used by every list endpoint.

post.description: Adds a department. The hospital is the session's: the body carries no tenant. A name already used by a department of the hospital, archived or not, whatever its capitals, is refused with 409 department_name_taken.

parameters.name: idempotency-key
parameters.description: A unique value (such as a UUID) chosen by the client. Repeating the request with the same key returns the first result instead of doing the work again.

201.description: A department of one hospital. Holds no patient data.

patch.description: Changes a department. Send the version the change was made from: 409 conflict when the department has changed since, 409 department_name_taken for a name in use. Sending what the department already has changes nothing. A department of another hospital answers 404 department_not_found, the same as one that does not exist.

200.description: A department of one hospital. Holds no patient data.

post.description: Archives a department: it stays on the records that name it and is no longer offered for new ones. Doing it twice changes nothing. A department of another hospital answers 404 department_not_found, the same as one that does not exist.

200.description: A department of one hospital. Holds no patient data.

post.description: Brings an archived department back. Doing it twice changes nothing. A department of another hospital answers 404 department_not_found, the same as one that does not exist.

200.description: A department of one hospital. Holds no patient data.

get.description: Active staff members of the active tenant who have no doctor profile yet, by name: who a profile can be created for. `q` matches the name or the email address. Staff are users, not patients.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: Opaque. Pass the nextCursor of the previous page.

200.description: Cursor envelope used by every list endpoint.

get.description: Doctors of the active tenant, by name. `q` matches the name or the specialization. `total` comes with the first page.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: Opaque. Pass the nextCursor of the previous page.

parameters.name: active
parameters.description: False lists the doctors who are no longer active instead.

200.description: Cursor envelope used by every list endpoint.

post.description: Gives a staff member of the hospital a doctor profile. The hospital is the session's: the body carries no tenant. 409 doctor_exists when that person already has one, 400 when the user is not an active member or the department is not an active department of the hospital.

The first price of a service may start today at the hospital (its timezone) or later. Once a price is in force, a new one starts tomorrow or later, never today: charges posted this morning used the price that was in force. Every change is audited with who made it, and the event names the fields that changed; a change of `schedule` or `controlled` is audited as `reclassify`, so taking an item out of a controlled schedule leaves its own trace, and an item that is not controlled, renamed or moved to a form in which the hospital has a controlled item of the same generic name, is audited a second time as `beside_controlled`. Records that name an item keep what it was: a dispense, a stock entry and a prescription line store the generic name, brand, form, strength, schedule and controlled flag as they were when the line was written, so renaming or reclassifying an item never changes history. get.description: The reference range that applies to a patient of an age and a sex: the row for that sex covering that age, else the row for any sex covering it, else none. A patient whose sex is recorded as other gets only a row for any. It answers the check on the catalog screen with an age someone typed, and identifies no patient: the age is tried as that of a person born on 1 January 2001, so 30 days is under one month. It is not how a result is read for a real patient: the laboratory works that out on the server from the date of birth of the patient of the order and the date the sample was collected, with the same rule (a limit is reached on the calendar day that lies that long after the birth; a month or a year lands on the same day of the month, or on the last day of a shorter month), and the age or date of birth of a patient is never sent in an address. A test of another hospital answers 404 lab_test_not_found, the same as one that does not exist.

200.description: `range` is absent when no row covers that age and sex.

200.description: Default Response

put.description: Replaces the reference ranges of a test. Only a numeric single test has ranges (409 lab_test_has_no_ranges for a panel or a text test). Each row gives at least one limit, `low` below `high`, a critical limit never inside the normal range, and an `ageUntil` that is later than `ageFrom` for every date of birth. Two rows for the same sex must never both hold for a patient: one has to end at or before the age the other starts from, for every date of birth. Years and months compare exactly with each other, and weeks and days with each other; a limit in months or years against one in weeks or days is accepted only when no date of birth can bring them together (a month is 28 to 31 days), so ranges that meet give the age in the same unit. A row for one sex and a row for any may share ages, and the one for the sex is used. 400 otherwise. 409 conflict when the ranges have changed since the version sent. A limit is a number: one sent as null or as text is refused, never read as 0. A result already reported keeps the range it was reported against. Audited. A test of another hospital answers 404 lab_test_not_found, the same as one that does not exist.

post.description: Diagnosis and procedure codes, searched on the server: the code sets are large and are never sent whole or bundled into the web app. It reads data only. The search term travels in the body, never in a query string: it is free text typed while a patient's record may be open, and a diagnosis term beside a patient id in an access log is patient data. The API does not log the body. The codes themselves are the same for every hospital; `favourite` is the active tenant's own mark, taken from the session, never from the client. `q` is words in any order: each matches the start of the code (with or without its dot) or the start of a word of the title. The hospital's favourites come first, then the other codes, each in the order of the codes. `favourites: true` gives the favourites only, which is what a search box shows before anything is typed. `total` comes with the first page only. The answer is the active tenant's view and is private to the session: `Cache-Control: private, no-store`.

get.description: The document templates of the active tenant, by name: each hospital has its own. Requires template:read and the templates feature flag. `total` comes with the first page only.

parameters.name: archived
parameters.description: True lists the archived templates instead of the ones in use.

200.description: Cursor envelope used by every list endpoint.

post.description: Adds a template, as its version 1. Requires template:manage and template:read. The hospital is the session’s. The kind cannot be changed later. A name another template of the same kind has at the hospital, archived or not, whatever the capitals, is refused with 409 template_name_taken. The body is not empty, and every placeholder in it is one the kind of template knows (400 otherwise): patient.name, patient.mrn, patient.age, patient.sex, doctor.name, hospital.name and date.today for every kind; procedure.name for a consent form; admission.date and discharge.date for a discharge summary. A template is a blank form: it holds no patient data, and a placeholder is filled in only when a document is made from it. Audited. A repeat with the same Idempotency-Key adds nothing and answers with the template as it is now.

parameters.name: idempotency-key
parameters.description: A unique value (such as a UUID) chosen by the client. Repeating the request with the same key returns the first result instead of doing the work again.

get.description: One template with the text of its newest version and the list of every version it has had. Requires template:read. A template of another hospital answers 404 template_not_found, the same as one that does not exist.

200.description: Default Response

put.description: Saves a new version of a template: the name, the text, or both. Requires template:manage and template:read. Versions are append-only: nothing saved is ever changed or removed, except by a redaction, and a document made from a template keeps the version it was made from. Send the version the change was made from: 409 conflict when a newer one has been saved since. Saving what the newest version already has makes no new version. An archived template is read-only: 409 template_archived until it is restored. A template has at most 500 versions (409 template_version_limit), the last of which only someone who holds template:redact may save, so that a correction is always possible. The body is not empty, and every placeholder in it is one the kind of template knows (400 otherwise): patient.name, patient.mrn, patient.age, patient.sex, doctor.name, hospital.name and date.today for every kind; procedure.name for a consent form; admission.date and discharge.date for a discharge summary. A template is a blank form: it holds no patient data, and a placeholder is filled in only when a document is made from it. Audited. A template of another hospital answers 404 template_not_found, the same as one that does not exist.

200.description: Default Response

get.description: The name and text of one version of a template, as it was saved. Requires template:read. 404 template_version_not_found for a version it never had. A redacted version answers with an empty name and text, and when, by whom and why it was redacted. A template of another hospital answers 404 template_not_found, the same as one that does not exist.

200.description: One version of a template, as it was saved. A redacted version has an empty name and an empty text, and says when, by whom and why.

post.description: Removes the name and the text of one older version of a template, for when something was typed into it that should not be kept: a real patient’s details, say. It is the one change ever made to a saved version, and it cannot be undone. The version stays in the history with its number, who saved it and when, and who redacted it, when and why; the reason is from a list. Requires template:redact and template:read. The newest version is the template as it is used, so it is not redacted (409 template_version_current): save a corrected version first, and restore an archived template to do so. Redacting a version twice changes nothing. A document already made from the version keeps its own text. Audited. 404 template_version_not_found for a version it never had. A template of another hospital answers 404 template_not_found, the same as one that does not exist.

200.description: Default Response

post.description: Archives a template: it is no longer offered for a new document. Documents made from it keep their text. Requires template:manage and template:read. Doing it twice changes nothing, and neither makes a new version. Audited. A template of another hospital answers 404 template_not_found, the same as one that does not exist.

200.description: Default Response

post.description: Brings an archived template back. Requires template:manage and template:read. Doing it twice changes nothing, and neither makes a new version. Audited. A template of another hospital answers 404 template_not_found, the same as one that does not exist.

200.description: Default Response

200.description: Records of one kind loaded from a file. It holds counts and codes, never a value of a row.

post.description: Adds rows to a batch that is being staged, up to 20000 in all (409 import_too_many_rows). A line already sent is kept as it was first sent, so a chunk sent again adds nothing. The rows can be patient data: the API does not log the body, and they are deleted once the batch is written, refused or given up. Audited. A batch of another hospital answers 404 import_not_found, the same as one that does not exist.

200.description: Records of one kind loaded from a file. It holds counts and codes, never a value of a row.

post.description: Starts the dry run of a staged batch: a job checks every row as its create route would, and writes nothing. Follow its progress on the batch; its problems are then in the report. 409 import_empty for a batch with no rows. A batch of another hospital answers 404 import_not_found, the same as one that does not exist.

202.description: Records of one kind loaded from a file. It holds counts and codes, never a value of a row.

post.description: Writes a checked batch with no problems (409 import_not_ready otherwise): a job writes every row in one transaction, each audited and announced as its create route does, so the batch is all of its rows or none. A row refused at that moment (the catalog changed since the check) fails the whole batch, with its report. One batch is written at a time at a hospital (409 import_running). Audited. A batch of another hospital answers 404 import_not_found, the same as one that does not exist.

202.description: Records of one kind loaded from a file. It holds counts and codes, never a value of a row.

post.description: Gives up a batch that is staged or checked: its rows are deleted and nothing is written. A batch whose job is running is not given up (409 import_busy). Cancelling twice changes nothing. Audited. A batch of another hospital answers 404 import_not_found, the same as one that does not exist.

get.description: The report of a batch: what is wrong with which line and field, in the order of the lines. Codes only, never a value of the file. A batch of another hospital answers 404 import_not_found, the same as one that does not exist.

post.description: Opens a deep link to a record by its globally unique id. The server finds the hospital that owns the record, checks that the user is an active member of it, and rebinds the session to that hospital if another one (or none) is active. Every refusal is the same 403 link_unavailable, whether the record does not exist or belongs to a hospital the user does not work at, so a link cannot be used to find out what exists.

get.description: The appointments of the active tenant that start on the days from `from` to `to` (calendar days at the hospital, both included, at most 31 days), by start time then id. Filtered by doctor and by status. A list, not a search: nothing in its address is typed about a patient, so it is a GET. Each row names its patient (name and MRN) for anyone who may read appointments. The scope of the caller's `appointment:read` is applied on the server, whatever the filters say: with scope `own`, only the appointments of the caller's own doctor profile are returned, a `doctorId` of another doctor gives an empty page (not a refusal that would tell anything), and `total` counts only what the caller may see. The default grant to doctors is the whole hospital (scope all); the web app opens on the signed-in doctor's own schedule, which is a default of the screen, not a limit. Every page read is audited, with the actor and the ids of the appointments returned. `total` comes with the first page only. Planned with the appointments API (#75).

parameters.description: The first day, at the hospital.

parameters.name: to

parameters.name: doctorId
parameters.description: Only this doctor's appointments.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: Opaque. Pass the nextCursor of the previous page.
